q: O'ercome with shame, and loaded with disgrace,
1838, Thomas Eagles, Brendallah, A Poem, Whittaker & Co., section LXX, page 115:
And that very night, as we lay packed tight in our robes beneath the snow, / And the dogs were fed, and the stars o'erhead were dancing heel and toe...
1907, Robert Service, “The Cremation of Sam McGee”, in The Spell of The Yukon and Other Verses:

We see him now — the old slouched hat cocked o’er his eye askew,
The shrewd, dry smile, the speech so pat, so calm, so blunt, so true.

1712, The Rape of the Lock by Alexander Pope, quotee, “A Key to the Lock”, in Law is a Bottomless Pit. Or, the History of John Bull., page 240:

But if vile Rancour, from (no Matter who)
 Actor, or Mimic, Printer, or Review,
 Lies oft o’erthrown with ceaſeleſs Venom ſpread,
 Still hiſs out Scandal from their Hydra Head,
 If the dull Malice boldly walk the Town,
 Patience herſelf wou’d wrinkle to a Frown.
1761, R[obert] Lloyd, An Epistle to C. Churchill, Author of the Rosciad, London: […] William Flexney, […], pages 7–8:
The Prince of Cumberland! that is a step / On which I must fall down, or else o'erleap, / For in my way it lies.

I have no spur / To prick the sides of my intent, but only / Vaulting ambition, which o'erleaps itself / And falls on th' other.
